title: refactor(ci): split lint/test/release workflows, optimize cache, bump GH Actions
author: Ava Martinez
description:
Motivation: Our single monolithic CI workflow has grown slow and brittle as we added more checks and cross-language targets. This PR splits responsibilities into focused workflows (lint, test, release) to reduce PR latency, enable independent caching strategies, and make release automation more reliable. It also modernizes our GH Actions usage (checkout/setup-node), tightens cache keys for node/npm/pnpm, and extracts common steps into a composite action to reduce duplication.

What I changed: consolidated CI logic into three workflows: .github/workflows/lint.yml, .github/workflows/test.yml, .github/workflows/release.yml. Added a reusable composite action at .github/actions/ci-helpers to centralize checkout, install-cache-restore, and setup tooling. Improved cache keys to avoid cross-branch corruption and added restore-keys to improve hit rates for transient branch work. Bumped GH Actions versions (actions/checkout@v4, actions/setup-node@v4) and normalized node matrix (18, 20) with default 20 for new packages. Tightened release workflow to run full test matrix on scheduled nightly and to gate manual release runs with a verified CI pass.

Checklist:
- [x] Split lint/test/release into separate workflows with minimal overlapping steps
- [x] Add composite action for shared CI steps
- [x] Add deterministic cache keys and restore-keys for node_modules and build caches
- [x] Bump actions to v4 and remove deprecated steps
- [x] Keep small PRs fast by limiting heavy jobs to nightly/scheduled runs
- [x] Update docs/README.ci.md with new workflow guidance

Testing and rollout: I iterated on this branch with several CI runs to validate cache hits and parallelism improvements. Early runs showed ~30% faster PR feedback on average for SDK packages and docs builds due to parallel lint/test jobs and better cache locality. Release workflow was tested on a dry-run tag using release-candidate mode; manual approvals required for production release.

Notes/risks: There are a few legacy projects that still rely on the old monolithic assumptions (custom scripts invoking ci.yml). I left a compatibility note in README.ci.md and created a Linear task (ENG-1254) to follow up and update those scripts. Some flaky integration tests were temporarily moved to nightly to avoid blocking fast PRs; they remain in the test matrix for nightly coverage.

Related: Linear ENG-1254, ENG-1302. See internal runbook: docs/ci/runbook.md for troubleshooting cache keys and matrix failures.
